title: Eid Al Etihad 2026: A Guide to UAE National Day
summary: UAE National Day falls on Wed., Dec. 2, 2026. Learn what Eid Al Etihad means, how the Emirates celebrate, and what to know before visiting.
body_markdown:
***Quick answer:** Eid Al Etihad, also known as UAE National Day, falls on Wednesday, December 2, 2026. It marks 55 years since six emirates united to form the United Arab Emirates in 1971. Ras Al Khaimah joined in 1972, bringing the total to seven. The name means “Celebration of the Union,” and festivities include cultural performances, community events, and displays in the colors of the UAE flag.*


**A friend living in Dubai sends you a video. Skyscrapers glow red, green, white, and black against the night sky, and the streets are full of music and flags. You might wonder what’s behind it all.**


**That celebration is Eid Al Etihad, or UAE National Day, and it’s one of the most meaningful dates on the Emirati calendar. Whether you have family or friends in the UAE, you’re planning a December trip to Dubai or Abu Dhabi, or you’re simply curious about the holiday lighting up your social feed, this guide breaks down what Eid Al Etihad means, when it falls in 2026, and how people mark the occasion.**


## When is Eid Al Etihad in 2026?


Eid Al Etihad lands on Wednesday, December 2, 2026. For anyone planning a visit or trying to reach someone in the UAE, here’s how the holiday breaks down across different sectors:


**What readers are looking for** **2026 dates**


UAE National Day Wednesday, December 2


Paid holiday for private-sector employees Wednesday–Thursday, December 2–3


Holiday for federal government employees Wednesday–Friday, December 2–4


The UAE’s[Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation](https://www.mohre.gov.ae/en/home.aspx) confirms the private-sector holiday dates, while the Federal Authority for Government Human Resources sets the schedule for federal employees. Individual emirates, businesses, and attractions may adjust their hours around the holiday, so if you’re trying to reach a specific office or visit an attraction, check that venue’s posted hours directly.


## What does Eid Al Etihad mean?


Eid Al Etihad translates to “Celebration of the Union.” In Arabic, it’s written عيد الاتحاد. You’ll often see it paired with “UAE National Day” in English-language coverage, since both names refer to the same holiday.


The story behind the name is short, but it carries real weight. On December 2, 1971, six emirates—Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Ajman, Umm Al Quwain, and Fujairah—came together to form the United Arab Emirates. Ras Al Khaimah joined a few months later, on February 10, 1972, completing the union of seven emirates that exists today. Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, widely regarded as the UAE’s founding president, led this unification and remains central to how the country tells its own story each year on this date.


## How do people celebrate UAE National Day?


Eid Al Etihad celebrations typically combine large public events with smaller, neighborhood-level gatherings. Two confirmed examples from 2026 show the range of what’s planned.


### What happens at Dubai’s light shows?


Visit Dubai has listed free evening light shows at Bluewaters Island and The Beach, JBR, scheduled for 8 p.m. and 10 p.m. UAE time on December 2 and 3. The program includes traditional Emirati performances alongside the light displays, making it an accessible option for visitors who want to experience the holiday without needing tickets or reservations. Since event details can shift, check Visit Dubai’s listings closer to the date to confirm times and access.


### What’s happening in Abu Dhabi’s neighborhoods?


Abu Dhabi takes a more community-centered approach. The Department of Municipalities and Transport has announced celebrations in Khalifa City, Al Shamkha City, and Al Falah City running from December 1 to 3. These neighborhood events are worth noting if you’re staying outside the main tourist areas or want a sense of how residents celebrate close to home, rather than at a large public venue.


Across the UAE, expect similar touches wherever you go: performances rooted in Emirati heritage, community gatherings, and buildings, parks, and public spaces decorated in the UAE flag’s colors—red, green, white, and black.


## How can you mark Eid Al Etihad from the US?


You don’t need to be in the Emirates to take part. A simple message—”Happy UAE National Day!”—to a friend, colleague, or family member living there goes a long way. Asking how their neighborhood is celebrating this year is also a natural way to connect, especially since celebrations vary so much by city and community.


If you want to follow the official festivities, the Eid Al Etihad website (eidaletihad.ae) is the best source for ceremony updates, including this year’s “Our Celebration, Made Together” initiative and the 55th Eid Al Etihad song playlist, available on YouTube, Apple Music, and Spotify. If organizers announce a broadcast for the 2026 ceremony, the official site is where that information will appear first. Since the UAE operates on UAE Standard Time (UTC+4), keep that offset in mind when converting any announced times to your local US time zone.


## Frequently asked questions about Eid Al Etihad


### Is Eid Al Etihad the same as UAE National Day?


Yes. Eid Al Etihad is the official name for the UAE’s annual national celebration held every December 2. “UAE National Day” is simply the common English-language term for the same holiday.


### How is Eid Al Etihad different from Eid Al Fitr and Eid Al Adha?


Eid Al Etihad commemorates the founding of the UAE and always falls on a fixed Gregorian calendar date: December 2. Eid Al Fitr and Eid Al Adha, by contrast, are religious holidays tied to the Islamic lunar calendar, so their dates shift each year relative to the Gregorian calendar, according to the UAE’s official government portal, u.ae.


### Can tourists join Eid Al Etihad celebrations?


Yes. Many Eid Al Etihad events are open to the public, including the free evening light shows in Dubai at Bluewaters Island and The Beach, JBR. For the most current times and access details, check directly with the event organizer before you go, since schedules can change closer to the holiday.


### What’s the best way to budget for a December trip to the UAE?


If Eid Al Etihad coincides with travel plans, expect higher demand for flights and hotels around December 1–4, when both private-sector and federal holidays overlap. Booking accommodations and transport early can help you secure better rates during this period.


## Bringing the celebration home


Eid Al Etihad is a reminder of how far the UAE has come since six emirates first joined forces in 1971, and how that founding spirit still shapes daily life across the Emirates today. Whether you’re watching a light show in Dubai, reading about neighborhood gatherings in Abu Dhabi, or simply sending a message to someone celebrating thousands of miles away, there are plenty of ways to be part of the moment.
